regime: Risk-Off Flush (Downtrend, Rotation to Metals and Energy)
summary: The pullback turned into a flush. With nothing on the calendar, the indices leaned on Friday's short flip and sold off, both closing under their falling trend stops near the session lows. MNQ closed -0.25% at 30,080 and MES -0.47% at 7,766, each below its stop and its average. VIX popped 6.6% to 15.19, so risk came off across the board, but off a low base, so this reads as broad de-risking rather than a fear event. The other side of the tape was strong: gold added 0.93% to 4,440 and crude ripped 3.08% to 84.95 on the geopolitical premium, so money rotated out of stocks and into metals and energy.
psychology: Friday flipped the trend stops short. Today the market followed through. If you spent the session hunting a bottom to buy, you were fighting a falling stop the whole way down. Here is the discipline piece. A trend flip is a change of plan. Do not treat it as a dip to fade. When your stop flips short, your job is to trade the short or stand aside. Guessing the low is how an account bleeds, because the bottom is obvious in hindsight and expensive in real time. Let price reclaim the stop before you trust the long side again.
